audience.programmeDescription: Educational Sciences at the University of Amsterdam studies how people learn and how education can improve. Students examine learning environments, educational organisations and policy, and develop skills in educational research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in learning and development, cognition and technology, or workplace development and leadership. UvA provides dedicated study of curriculum, instruction and educational assessment, followed by an 18 EC empirical thesis.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENBUSI211.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
BENBUSI211.text: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. Students study AI's capabilities and limits, applications across business functions and industries, and effects on labour markets, productivity, innovation and inequality. Business cases and scholarly arguments support analysis of governance, regulation and a country's AI readiness and industrial policy.

BENECON311.text: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.

BENENTR212.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
BENENTR212.text: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.

BENGATE101.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
BENGATE101.text: Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.

BENGATE102.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

BENLEAD111.text: Introduces self-leadership, leadership theory and emotional intelligence. Students use personality and emotional-intelligence profiles to reflect on group dynamics, study leadership cases, and develop a personal plan with practical goals. Assessment tools support educational reflection, with attention to differences in their scientific support.

BENLEAD211.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
BENLEAD211.text: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership in diverse contexts, with particular attention to minority experiences. Students design and pilot a quantitative survey, collect data ethically, and use SPSS or RStudio for descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression. They interpret the findings and develop evidence-based leadership recommendations.

BENLEAD312.text: How do you get to yes? In this course you will learn how to craft persuasive arguments, deploy the right language, negotiate more effectively, and influence decisions with confidence—whether in business, leadership, or life.

DISARIN111.text: AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness, privacy, responsibility, human-value alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Students apply ethical frameworks to questions about human behaviour and interaction, synthesise research in an analytical psychology project, and produce a research-based podcast.

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.text: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
